headline: TALON HITS THICKEST TAMARACK INTERCEPT YET — Step-outs expand 138 Zone footprint, Vault Zone drill confirms nickel-copper-cobalt system extends
snippet: Talon Metals (TSX: TLO) reported the thickest 138 Zone intercept in Tamarack's exploration history on November 11, with drill hole 25TK0563 intersecting two intervals of massive sulphide and matrix massive sulphide carrying high-grade nickel, copper and precious metals. Additional step-out drilling near the Vault Zone confirms the nickel-copper-cobalt mineralizing system is broader than previously defined, adding geological scale to what is already the most advanced domestic nickel project in the United States and a critical battery-metal supply-chain asset.

headline: INDIA BANS LITHIUM BATTERY BLACK MASS EXPORTS OVERNIGHT — Recycled Li/Co/Ni/Mn reclassified from 'free' to 'prohibited' with immediate effect
snippet: India changed its export classification for lithium-ion battery black mass — a recycled intermediate containing lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese — from 'free' to 'prohibited' effective immediately on November 11, cutting off a stream of secondary critical mineral feedstock from global supply chains. The overnight policy reversal reflects India's intent to build a domestic battery recycling and refining industry, but removes a low-cost cobalt and nickel source that Asian cathode manufacturers had relied on as primary prices remained elevated.

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD M&I RESOURCES JUMP 38% — 27.3M tonnes at 2.19 g/t Au after Dropkick Zone added to Queensway estimate
snippet: New Found Gold (TSX: NFGC) reported in its Q3 2026 results that measured and indicated resources at the Queensway Project in Newfoundland grew 38% to 27.3 million tonnes averaging 2.19 g/t gold, driven largely by the addition of the Dropkick Zone. The upgrade marks a meaningful step toward the resource scale needed to attract major-company attention in a M&A environment where senior gold producers — sitting on record cash flow from $4,000/oz gold — are actively looking for high-grade development-stage assets in Tier-1 jurisdictions.

headline: CHINA EXTENDS RARE EARTH EXPORT WAIVERS 2 MONTHS — USAR rebounds 11%, MP Materials climbs 4% on relief rally
snippet: China announced on November 9 a two-month extension of rare earth export-control waivers that were due to expire on November 10, temporarily lifting a supply-shock risk that had been pressuring Western rare earth equities. The relief drove USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) up 11% on November 11 from its Q3-miss lows, with MP Materials (NYSE: MP) recovering 4% and United States Antimony edging higher. Analysts caution the extension is a reprieve, not a resolution — China retains the structural leverage to restrict exports at any renewal date, keeping the case for domestic rare earth production intact.

headline: USA RARE EARTH Q3 MISS: $3M REVENUE VS $13.5M FORECAST — Adjusted loss widens; first magnet sales confirmed but scale far from analyst models
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) reported Q3 2026 revenue of approximately $3 million against a consensus estimate of $13.55 million, with an adjusted loss of $0.44 per share versus the expected $0.146 loss — triggering an 11% single-day selloff on November 10 and dragging Energy Fuels (UUUU) down 8% and MP Materials (MP) 5% in sympathy. Management confirmed first commercial rare earth magnet sales from Serra Verde in Brazil, but the revenue gap highlights how much longer the production ramp is taking than analysts anticipated when the stock was pricing in a faster path to profitability.

headline: RIO TINTO EXPANDS US RESOLUTION COPPER — Domestic supply chain push accelerates at Arizona's giant 1.9B-tonne porphyry deposit
snippet: Rio Tinto announced an expansion of its Resolution Copper project in Arizona — hosting one of the largest undeveloped copper deposits in the world at 1.9 billion tonnes — to strengthen the US domestic copper supply chain, according to SMM's morning market summary. Resolution's advancement is a Washington priority under the critical minerals executive order, and any expansion of scope or capital commitment there narrows the structural copper deficit that physical buyers in China and Western Europe have been scrambling to manage through record import premiums.

headline: FREEPORT-McMoRAN SHARES JUMP 3% AS COPPER HOLDS 2026 GAINS — Tight physical market underpins world's largest copper miner while oil drops 7.6%
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) shares gained 3% on November 11 as copper held its roughly 15.6% year-to-date gain — a standout performance against oil's 7.6% decline and lithium's 21% month-over-month crash. The divergence between copper's resilience and other commodity weakness reinforces the structural deficit thesis: Freeport, which produces approximately 4 billion pounds of copper annually across its US, South American and Indonesian operations, is the most direct equity expression of that thesis, and institutional buyers are positioning ahead of what several bank analysts see as a supply-demand crunch accelerating into 2027.

headline: ARGENTINA TO CLAIM SOUTH AMERICAN LITHIUM CROWN FROM CHILE BY 2035 — Cochilco also cuts Chile's 2026 copper output forecast 8.4% to 4.9M tonnes
snippet: A Mining.com analysis projects Argentina will overtake Chile as South America's largest lithium producer by 2035, driven by brine development across Salta and Jujuy provinces as Chile's Atacama brine resources face tighter water management regulations and slower project approvals. Separately, Chile's state copper commission Cochilco cut its 2026 copper production forecast by 8.4% to 4.9 million tonnes, citing aging mine grades, water stress and permitting delays — a supply-side signal that reinforces the structural deficit thesis even as macro headwinds suppress short-term futures prices.

headline: GDX RALLIES 20% FROM LOWS — Oversold signals flash bigger gains ahead as gold stabilizes near $4,000
snippet: An Investing.com technical analysis argues the Gold Miners ETF (GDX) has already bounced 20% from its recent lows and that multiple oversold indicators — RSI divergence, historically low P/NAV multiples across senior producers, and unusually high short interest — suggest the recovery has further to run as gold stabilizes near $4,000. The piece targets GDX at $105 and eventual all-time highs, drawing a parallel to the 2015-2016 miner recovery cycle, though it notes that any further macro shock (another CPI miss, rate hike surprise) could cut the rally short before the structural thesis reasserts.

headline: CAMECO LEADS URANIUM STOCKS AS SPOT U₃O₈ HOLDS $91/LB — Kazakhstan building 100-year strategic reserve signals tight market ahead
snippet: An Admiral Markets uranium sector overview for November 2026 highlights Cameco (NYSE: CCJ) as the benchmark uranium equity, trading near multi-year highs as spot U3O8 holds around $91 per pound. The piece flags Kazakhstan's directive to build a strategic uranium reserve to cover more than 100 years of planned domestic nuclear needs as a market-tightening signal — Kazatomprom is the world's largest uranium producer and any diversion of output to a national reserve reduces the volume available to global utilities already scrambling to replace Russian-sourced material under Western sanctions compliance programs.

headline: NORTHERNMINER SPOTLIGHT: FOUR US JUNIORS DRILL FOR SCALE — American jurisdiction gains traction as domestic supply-chain policy accelerates permitting
snippet: The Northern Miner's Part 2 of its US junior mining spotlight examines four domestic exploration companies drilling for multi-million-ounce scale in Nevada, Arizona and the Great Basin region, with the editorial framing anchored in Washington's accelerating push to develop US-sourced critical mineral and precious metal reserves. The piece argues that executive orders streamlining federal permitting on defense-critical deposits have materially changed the risk calculus for US-domiciled juniors compared to their Canadian and Australian peers — the traditionally lower US risk premium is being re-rated upward by institutional capital allocating to domestic-supply-chain themes.

headline: MONTAGE GOLD KONÉ MINE ON BUDGET AT $796M COMMITTED — 25-of-25 Q3 exploration targets return mineralization, Côte d'Ivoire
snippet: Montage Gold (TSX: MAU) reported Q3 2026 activities showing its Koné mine construction in Côte d'Ivoire remains on budget with $796.4 million of capital committed, while exploration drilling hit positive mineralization at all 25 targets drilled year-to-date — a 100% hit rate that significantly expands the district-scale resource potential surrounding the main deposit. Koné is on track to become one of West Africa's largest new gold mines, and the clean construction execution alongside systematic exploration success makes Montage one of the more fully de-risked mid-tier development stories in the current environment.
